speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To help me understand what is wrong, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been going on?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the baby is irritable with worsening pain upon palpation and reduced feeding. To determine if this is a surgical emergency, has he passed any stool or gas since the symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming; the absence of fever, vomiting, or diarrhea is notable. Given the distension, pain on touch, and lack of stool/gas passage, we must rule out an obstruction or volvulus. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia. The combination of an 8-month-old infant with feeding difficulties, abdominal distension, pain on palpation, and the absence of stool/gas, supported by X-ray findings of dilated bowel segments and no gas in the rectum, is highly indicative of a proximal small bowel obstruction, with duodenal atresia being a primary consideration given the failure to pass meconium or stool.
